thread:
Maya Chen: Quick design check — scorecard toolbar feels visually heavy. Primary 'Approve' reads same weight as the kebab menu, makes scanning noisy. Screenshot: https://imgur.com/xyz :thinking:
Owen Patel: Agreed. Maybe reduce CTA weight and use a solid primary only when an item is selected? cc @Sarah Li
Sarah Li: I prototyped two approaches: (A) reduce icon weight + subtle divider; (B) keep ghost primary until selection, then solid. I prefer B for density. Link: https://figma.com/proto/abc
Josh R: Accessibility callout — disabled/low-contrast states look borderline. WCAG normal text 4.5:1. Measured ~3.8 for gray #6B6B6B on white. We should bump it.
Maya Chen: Also let's not use color-only affordance. Add icon + clear focus outline for keyboard users :keyboard:
DesignBot: Automated color check: option A contrast = 4.2, option B contrast = 4.8. Recommendation: option B for better compliance.
Sarah Li: Option B sounds good. UX question: when multiple items selected, do we show single 'Approve (3)' on the CTA or keep a separate compact batch bar?
Owen Patel: Show 'Approve (3)' inline on primary and keep a compact batch bar pinned to top to avoid layout shift — less surprising on selection.
Josh R: Important: tab order must be preserved. If the batch bar appears, it should receive focus first to avoid keyboard surprise and ensure screen reader users are aware.
Maya Chen: I'll update mocks. Small copy nit: change 'Approve' -> 'Approve selected' when selection >1 for clarity.
Sarah Li: I prefer keeping the visible label short ('Approve') and adding an aria-label for clarity: `button aria-label="Approve selected items"` for screen readers.
Josh R: Edge case — what if user presses Enter while focused on toolbar action? Current pattern fires action immediately. For large batches (>10) we should surface a confirm modal.
Maya Chen: +1. Rule: show confirm modal if count > 10, showing summary of items. I'll add that to the spec. :thumbsup:
DesignBot: Accessibility reminder: ensure modal has a focus trap and that focus returns to the originating toolbar button after close.
Owen Patel: Great. Maya — can you upload updated frames and a small interaction spec by EOD so eng can review?
Maya Chen: Yep uploading now: https://figma.com/file/abc123 (updated frames + notes). Will add the keyboard flow and aria examples in the spec.
